leading_positions.synthesis: Both supporters propose Buchwald and Hartwig for Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling and treat Kosugi as a precursor to be acknowledged rather than a third laureate. Both name the 2010 cross-coupling prize as the main objection but read C-N coupling as distinct. Brzezinski and Chabes list it as an alternative, and Aili and Linke credit its clean attribution, but Chabes and Aqvist see it as an extension of an honoured field, and Aqvist ranks it outside his top eight.

Both propose Balasubramanian and Klenerman for massively parallel sequencing by synthesis, and both have dropped Rothberg from their configurations (Aili would accept a third name if the committee judged the whole field needed it). They agree on a narrow citation built on reversible-terminator chemistry. Shared reservations are whether sequencing counts as chemistry rather than biological technology and whether leaving out Rothberg, Mayer and Ju is acceptable. Aqvist ranks it sixth for the same attribution reason.

A single member (the chair, speaking as a participant) proposes Miyasaka, Snaith and Park for halide perovskite solar-cell absorbers. Aqvist and Zou list it as a first alternative and Sparr as a second, but no other member prefers it outright. Open points are stability and lead content, the three-name cut among six credited names, and whether it is materials physics or chemistry.

A two-part proposal: David R. Liu alone for base editing, and Car and Parrinello for first-principles molecular dynamics. B052 is also an alternative of Aili, Linke, Somfai and Zou, but Brzezinski, Chabes and Linke see the 2020 CRISPR prize and the short clinical record as a timing problem, and Kondo and Nishida complicate credit. B019 has no other explicit supporter.

A two-part proposal: Brangwynne and Hyman for liquid-like condensates, and Cullis alone for ionizable lipid nanoparticles. B058 is the most frequent alternative (Aili, Chabes, Linke, Aqvist, Somfai) but no other member prefers it outright, mainly because six credited names cannot be allocated within three seats and the 2023 Medicine prize may be read as covering mRNA delivery. Brzezinski and Linke question the evidence for condensates in living cells.

A single-member position for Gray and Winkler on long-range electron transfer in proteins. Aqvist calls it a clean pairing and Chabes ranked it fifth in his opening, but it is conceptual rather than technological, and Brzezinski notes possible bias from proximity to his own field.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate has a majority of five. Explicit first-choice parts are spread across B021 (2), B028 (2), B003 (1), B052/B019 (1), B044/B058 (1) and B017 (1).
B021 has the cleanest attribution of the contested leaders: Buchwald and Hartwig as a pair, with Kosugi treated as precursor by every member who addressed him.

B058 is widely respected scientifically and is the commonest alternative (Aili, Chabes, Linke, Aqvist), yet the credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is repeatedly called unresolved within three names.
Members who propose B028 agree on a narrow citation around sequencing by synthesis rather than a broad claim on massively parallel sequencing.

Aili, Chabes and Aqvist explicitly want citations anchored in a specific chemical principle (reversible-terminator chemistry, deaminase chemistry, first-principles dynamics) rather than clinical or commercial outcomes.
scientific_disputes: Whether B021 is a distinct discovery or an extension of the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize: Somfai and Zou say distinct (C-C versus C-N, ligand design); Chabes and Aqvist see it as incremental or a successful application of an existing principle.
Whether base editing (B052) is a new chemical principle (Aqvist) or a refinement of CRISPR (Chabes, Brzezinski); Linke accepts the chemistry but doubts readiness.
Whether sequencing (B028), perovskite photovoltaics (B003) and lipid nanoparticles (B058) are chemistry or are better read as technology, materials physics or pharmacology.
Whether liquid-like condensates (B044) are established as equilibrium phase separation in living cells (Sparr, Brzezinski, Linke raise this).
Whether the lasting contribution of Car-Parrinello (B019) is the method or the concept, given the practical shift to Born-Oppenheimer dynamics.
attribution_disputes: B021: two names (Buchwald, Hartwig) versus three with Kosugi.
B028: Balasubramanian and Klenerman versus adding Rothberg (454), Mayer or Ju; Chabes dropped Rothberg from his opening ballot while Aili accepts him conditionally.
B003: the proposed trio (Miyasaka, Snaith, Park) versus Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis, who are credited on the ballot but not in the preferred configuration.
B052: Liu alone (Aqvist) versus Liu with Komor and Gaudelli versus the independent Kondo and Nishida Target-AID work.
B058: Cullis alone (Sparr) versus the Vancouver group (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) and the MIT group (Anderson, Langer).
B044: Brangwynne and Hyman versus Rosen, Pappu and Mittag, whose multivalency work Sparr says gives the concept its quantitative backbone.
B017: Gray and Winkler as the experimental pair, with theory contributors (Marcus, Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton) outside the credited names.
maturity_disputes: B052: clinical evidence is still early and the 2020 CRISPR prize is close in time (Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke; Aqvist disputes this).
B003: efficiency has been reproduced widely, but operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved (Aili, Aqvist, Linke).
B058: the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modification may be read as already covering delivery (Aili, Sparr).
B044: the physiological evidence for condensates is still contested.
B021, B019 and B017 are mature, with decades of independent confirmation; the dispute there is novelty and breadth, not maturity.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member discloses a conflict requiring recusal on any shortlisted candidate.

Disclosed scientific proximity, not recusal: Aili and Sparr on lipid and peptide-membrane work (B058, B044); Aqvist on simulation methods (B019); Brzezinski on electron transfer (B017); Chabes on sequencing as a tool (B028); Linke on physics-side bias toward B003.
Disclosed institutional ties, not recusal: Lund colleagues (Linke, Somfai, Sparr) and Stockholm colleagues (Brzezinski, Zou); none involves a credited laureate.
questions_for_round2: Is C-N coupling a distinct discovery from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize? Can Somfai and Zou state the new principle (ligand design) so that Aqvist and Chabes can test it, and is Kosugi a precursor or a priority claim?
Does the committee treat sequencing by synthesis as chemistry? If so, is a two-name citation on reversible-terminator chemistry defensible without Rothberg, Mayer and Ju?
Can Aqvist explain why Komor and Gaudelli would be credited ahead of Kondo and Nishida on B052, and can the timing relative to the 2020 CRISPR prize be addressed with evidence rather than impression?
Can any member propose a defensible three-name allocation for B058, or should it be dropped as unresolvable? How much weight should the 2023 Medicine prize carry?
Is a two-part prize (B052 with B019, B044 with B058) preferred to a single coherent achievement, and what test of coherence should the committee apply?
For B003, can the committee settle the three-name cut among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis, and is stability a barrier at this stage?
Would B017 be considered by members who did not rank it, now that its attribution is described as clean, or does it remain a single-member position?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a fragmented committee with no emerging majority. The positions that lead on attribution (B021, B028, B017) are less often ranked as the broadest on impact, while the candidates with widest impact support (B058, B052, B003) carry unresolved credit or maturity questions. Round 2 should focus on the 2010-prize question for B021, the chemistry-versus-technology question for B028, and attribution for B058 and B052.
